title: Older and Wiser: The Marriage of Device Aging and Intellectual Property Protection of DNNs
problem: Deep neural networks like GPT-3 are kept secret due to high training costs and privacy concerns, but existing IP protection approaches require expensive circuit redesign that incurs significant area, energy, and latency overheads. There is a need for lightweight DNN IP protection without substantial hardware modification costs.
motivation: DNN models represent valuable intellectual property assets with billion-dollar training costs, making protection against model theft and unauthorized deployment critical for commercial viability.
method: The approach combines hardware and software by taking advantage of device aging—the natural, gradual slowdown and efficiency loss that computer chips experience over time. Instead of designing new security circuits, the method trains the neural network using Differential Orientation Fine-tuning (DOFT) to work correctly only on hardware with specific aging patterns. As the chip naturally degrades, the network's performance adapts to match, making the protected model functional only on aged hardware with the expected degradation characteristics. Since this protection uses degradation that happens automatically anyway, it costs essentially nothing to implement compared to traditional security circuits.
key_novelty: The single core idea is using the natural aging of computer chips—which happens automatically and costs nothing—as the IP protection mechanism for neural networks, combined with Differential Orientation Fine-tuning so the network only works on aged hardware with expected degradation patterns.
contributions: Novel approach exploiting device aging characteristics for DNN IP protection
Differential orientation fine-tuning (DOFT) technique for protection
Hardware-software co-design eliminating expensive circuit redesign
Reduced area, energy, and latency overhead compared to prior protection schemes
